parts.label: a
parts.text:
(a) By writing $\sin 3\theta$ as $\sin(2\theta+\theta)$, show that
$$\sin 3\theta = 3\sin\theta - 4\sin^3\theta.$$
(5)
parts.mark_scheme:
(a) $\sin 3\theta = \sin(2\theta+\theta) = \sin 2\theta\cos\theta + \cos 2\theta\sin\theta$ B1
$= 2\sin\theta\cos^2\theta + (1-2\sin^2\theta)\sin\theta$ B1 B1
$= 2\sin\theta - 2\sin^3\theta + \sin\theta - 2\sin^3\theta$ M1
$= 3\sin\theta - 4\sin^3\theta$ * cso A1 (5)

parts.label: b
parts.text:
(b) Given that $\sin\theta = \dfrac{\sqrt{3}}{4}$, find the exact value of $\sin 3\theta$.
(2)
parts.mark_scheme: (b) $\sin 3\theta = 3\times\dfrac{\sqrt{3}}{4} - 4\left(\dfrac{\sqrt{3}}{4}\right)^3 = \dfrac{3\sqrt{3}}{4} - \dfrac{3\sqrt{3}}{16} = \dfrac{9\sqrt{3}}{16}$ or exact equivalent M1 A1 (2)

(4)

parts.label: b
parts.text:
(b) Show that $x^2+x+1 > 0$ for all values of $x$.
(3)
parts.mark_scheme:
(b) $x^2+x+1 = \left(x+\dfrac{1}{2}\right)^2 + \dfrac{3}{4}$, $> 0$ for all values of $x$. M1 A1, A1 (3)
Alternative: $\dfrac{d}{dx}(x^2+x+1) = 2x+1 = 0 \Rightarrow x = -\dfrac{1}{2} \Rightarrow x^2+x+1 = \dfrac{3}{4}$ M1 A1
A parabola with positive coefficient of $x^2$ has a minimum $\Rightarrow x^2+x+1 > 0$ A1 (3). Accept equivalent arguments

parts.label: c
parts.text:

(1)

Hence $\mathrm{f}(x) > 0$ B1 (1)

(b) $x^2+x+1 = \left(x+\dfrac{1}{2}\right)^2 + \dfrac{3}{4}$, $> 0$ for all values of $x$. M1 A1, A1 (3)
Alternative: $\dfrac{d}{dx}(x^2+x+1) = 2x+1 = 0 \Rightarrow x = -\dfrac{1}{2} \Rightarrow x^2+x+1 = \dfrac{3}{4}$ M1 A1

(c) $\mathrm{f}(x) = \dfrac{\left(x+\frac{1}{2}\right)^2+\frac{3}{4}}{(x+2)^2}$

questions.stem:
Figure 1 shows an oscilloscope screen.
The curve shown on the screen satisfies the equation
$$y = \sqrt{3}\cos x + \sin x.$$

parts.label: a
parts.text:
(a) Express the equation of the curve in the form $y = R\sin(x+\alpha)$, where $R$ and $\alpha$ are constants, $R > 0$ and $0 < \alpha < \dfrac{\pi}{2}$.
(4)
parts.mark_scheme:
(a) $R^2 = (\sqrt{3})^2+1^2 \Rightarrow R = 2$ M1 A1
$\tan\alpha = \sqrt{3} \Rightarrow \alpha = \dfrac{\pi}{3}$ accept awrt 1.05 M1 A1 (4)

parts.label: b
parts.text:

(4)

$x+\text{their }\alpha = \dfrac{\pi}{6}\left(\dfrac{5\pi}{6},\dfrac{13\pi}{6}\right)$ A1
$x = \dfrac{\pi}{2}, \dfrac{11\pi}{6}$ accept awrt 1.57, 5.76 M1 A1 (4)

questions.stem:
The function $\mathrm{f}$ is defined by
$$\mathrm{f}: x \mapsto \ln(4-2x), \quad x<2 \text{ and } x \in \mathbb{R}.$$

parts.label: a
parts.text:
(a) Show that the inverse function of $\mathrm{f}$ is defined by
$$\mathrm{f}^{-1}: x \mapsto 2 - \dfrac{1}{2}\mathrm{e}^x$$
and write down the domain of $\mathrm{f}^{-1}$.
(4)
parts.mark_scheme:
(a) $y = \ln(4-2x)$
$\mathrm{e}^y = 4-2x$ leading to $x = 2 - \dfrac{1}{2}\mathrm{e}^y$ Changing subject and removing ln M1 A1
$y = 2 - \dfrac{1}{2}\mathrm{e}^x \Rightarrow \mathrm{f}^{-1} \mapsto 2-\dfrac{1}{2}\mathrm{e}^x$ * cso A1
Domain of $\mathrm{f}^{-1}$ is $x \in \mathbb{R}$ B1 (4)

parts.label: b
parts.text:
(b) Write down the range of $\mathrm{f}^{-1}$.
(1)
parts.mark_scheme: (b) Range of $\mathrm{f}^{-1}$ is $\mathrm{f}^{-1}(x) < 2$ (and $\mathrm{f}^{-1}(x) \in \mathbb{R}$) B1 (1)

parts.label: c
parts.text:
(c) In the space provided on page 16, sketch the graph of $y = \mathrm{f}^{-1}(x)$. State the coordinates of the points of intersection with the $x$ and $y$ axes.
(4)
parts.mark_scheme: (c) Sketch showing correct shape decreasing curve with asymptote $y=2$: Shape B1; intercept at $x = 1.5$ B1; intercept at $x = \ln 4$ B1; asymptote $y=2$ B1 (4)

parts.label: d
parts.text:
The graph of $y = x+2$ crosses the graph of $y = \mathrm{f}^{-1}(x)$ at $x=k$.
The iterative formula
$$x_{n+1} = -\dfrac{1}{2}\mathrm{e}^{x_n}, \quad x_0 = -0.3$$
is used to find an approximate value for $k$.
(d) Calculate the values of $x_1$ and $x_2$, giving your answers to 4 decimal places.
(2)
parts.mark_scheme:
(d) $x_1 \approx -0.3704$, $x_2 \approx -0.3452$ cao B1, B1 (2)
If more than 4 dp given in this part a maximum of one mark is lost. Penalise on the first occasion.

parts.label: e
parts.text:
(e) Find the value of $k$ to 3 decimal places.
(2)
parts.mark_scheme:
(e) $x_3 = -0.35403019$, $x_4 = -0.35092688$, $x_5 = -0.35201761$, $x_6 = -0.35163386$ Calculating to at least $x_6$ to at least four dp M1
$k \approx -0.352$ cao A1 (2)
Alternative: $k \approx -0.352$ Found in any way. Let $\mathrm{g}(x) = x+\dfrac{1}{2}\mathrm{e}^x$
$\mathrm{g}(-0.3515) \approx +0.0003$, $\mathrm{g}(-0.3525) \approx -0.001$ M1
Change of sign (and continuity) $\Rightarrow k \in (-0.3525,-0.3515)$
$\Rightarrow k = -0.352$ (to 3 dp) A1 (2)

parts.mark_scheme:

$= \tan^2 x - \cot^2 x$ * cso A1 (3)
Alternative: $\sec^2 x - \tan^2 x = 1 = \csc^2 x - \cot^2 x$
Rearranging $\sec^2 x - \csc^2 x = \tan^2 x - \cot^2 x$ * cso M1 A1 A1 (3)
Alternative: LHS $= \dfrac{1}{\cos^2 x} - \dfrac{1}{\sin^2 x} = \dfrac{\sin^2 x - \cos^2 x}{\cos^2 x \sin^2 x}$
RHS $= \dfrac{\sin^2 x}{\cos^2 x} - \dfrac{\cos^2 x}{\sin^2 x} = \dfrac{\sin^4 x - \cos^4 x}{\cos^2 x \sin^2 x} = \dfrac{(\sin^2 x-\cos^2 x)(\sin^2 x+\cos^2 x)}{\cos^2 x \sin^2 x}$ M1
$= \dfrac{\sin^2 x - \cos^2 x}{\cos^2 x \sin^2 x}$ A1
$=$ LHS * or equivalent A1 (3)
